name: EP-15 Business Hardening (Backlog)
w: Fix the business weak points found in docs/business-analysis.md: no way to charge yet, price-sensitive owners, expensive distribution, a long free trial, no product metrics, English-only, single-person operations and missing legal cover. Revenue features are in EP-14; this epic makes the business able to sell, measure and survive.
ac: Every weak point W1-W13 in docs/business-analysis.md has a task here or in EP-14
Activation, conversion, churn and cost per paying hostel are measured
Legal pack and backups are in place before the first 50 paying hostels
out: No second vertical (schools) until the gate in docs/business-analysis.md section W12 is met.
dod: Ideas only. Each task is detailed and estimated again when scheduled.

name: Product analytics and a metrics view in /admin
w: Weak point W8: without numbers, pricing and roadmap calls are guesses. Headline metric: rent recorded through the product each month.
ac: Track privacy-safe events (signup, import done, first allocation, first invoice run, payment recorded) with hostel ID only, no resident personal data
/admin shows activation, weekly active hostels, trial conversion and monthly churn
Each hostel records its acquisition channel, so cost per paying hostel can be worked out by channel
out: Needs a product analytics account (for example PostHog), or events stored in our own table.

name: Shorter trial with activation checkpoints
w: Weak point W5: a 90-day free trial delays cash and lets owners drift. A 30-day trial with clear checkpoints converts faster and shows willingness to pay early.
ac: Default trial is 30 days; /admin can still grant 90 days to launch partners
Activation is defined (beds imported, residents allocated, one invoice run) and shown per hostel
Hostels not activated by day 7 and day 21 are listed in /admin for a call
Owner sees a trial checklist on the dashboard

name: Paid done-for-you onboarding
w: Weak points W1 and W5: owners who pay something early convert better, and setup is the costliest part of a sale. A one-time setup fee, waived for annual prepayment, covers it.
ac: Setup fee and what it includes are written down (import, room setup, one training call)
Fee is waived when the owner prepays a year
Onboarding checklist in /admin marks each step done
out: Automatic charging of the fee: that comes with E14-T1.

name: Money-lost dashboard and monthly owner email
w: Weak point W2: owners compare the fee with a free notebook. Showing the rupees lost to empty beds and late rent makes the fee look small.
ac: Dashboard shows this month's lost rent from vacant priced beds and overdue invoices, in rupees
Monthly email to the owner with the same figures and the change since last month
Figures match the fees and occupancy pages exactly
out: Forecasting and benchmarks against other hostels.

name: Hindi UI, then the first cluster's language
w: Weak point W9: many owners and wardens are more comfortable in Hindi or a regional language.
ac: All UI text moved into message files; English stays the default
Hindi translation reviewed by a native speaker
Owner picks the language in settings; receipts follow the hostel's language
Second language added for the first sales cluster
out: Translating data the owner typed (room names, notes).

name: Legal pack: terms, privacy policy, data-processing agreement
w: Weak point W11: the product stores KYC documents and will handle payments. One complaint or data incident without legal cover is a serious liability.
ac: Lawyer-reviewed terms of service and privacy policy, linked from signup and the footer
Data-processing agreement with the owner as data fiduciary and us as processor, accepted at signup
Written breach-response plan with who does what within 72 hours
GST registration done before billing starts
out: Needs a lawyer familiar with the DPDP Act, 2023.

name: Marketing site and self-serve signup funnel
w: Weak point W4: referral and channel leads must be able to start without a sales visit. This was a deferred MVP gap.
ac: Landing page in English and Hindi with pricing, FAQ (including the private-ledger promise from W3) and case studies
Signup starts a trial and lands in onboarding
Each signup records its channel or referral code
Page loads fast on a low-end phone over 4G

name: Channel partner programme
w: Weak point W4: field sales cost too much against what each hostel pays. PG brokers, accountants, owner associations and suppliers already know owners.
ac: Written commission terms (for example a share of the first year's fees)
Partner codes tracked in /admin with signups and paid hostels per partner
Partner kit: one-page leaflet, demo video and WhatsApp messages in local languages
First three partners signed in the pilot area

name: Owner mobile flow and installable app
w: Weak point W9: owners and wardens work on their phones. The three daily jobs must be quick there.
ac: App can be installed from the browser (web app manifest and icons)
Record a payment, allocate a bed and see who is overdue in three taps or fewer from the home screen
Usable on a 360px-wide screen over slow 3G
out: Full offline mode and native app-store apps.

name: Backups, restore drill, uptime alerts and status page
w: Weak point W10: one lost database or a week of downtime at month-end, when rent is due, ends trust for good.
ac: Daily backups kept for at least 30 days, stored outside the main provider
Restore tested end to end and the steps written in docs
Uptime and error alerts reach the operator's phone
Public status page
out: Needs a paid Supabase plan (point-in-time recovery) or an external backup store, and a monitoring account.

name: Self-serve help and WhatsApp support
w: Weak point W10: support at this price cannot rely on one person answering calls.
ac: Short how-to videos in English and Hindi for the ten most common jobs
Help link on every page goes to the matching article
WhatsApp support number with a stated response time and saved replies
Support questions tagged so the most common ones become fixes or articles

name: Launch-partner case studies and testimonials
w: Weak point W13: owners trust other owners, not software claims.
ac: Two or three case studies with before-and-after numbers (overdue rent, vacant beds, time saved)
Short video testimonials in the local language, with written permission to use them
Used on the marketing site and in the channel partner kit
